report.source_text:
Immediate treatment with calcium gluconate and magnesium sulphate intravenously was given in the emergency department while monitoring the patient’s heart. Quickly after administration of calcium, his voice improved.
We admitted the patient to the acute care unit where he continued to receive calcium intravenously together with alphacalcidol (1 μg) since his blood test showed hypoparathyroidism and cholecalciferol orally to restore his vitamin D concentration. After 24 hours, he received 20 mmol calcium in total, which resulted in plasma calcium of 1.57 mmol/L (reference range: 2.20–2.65 mmol/L) and a normal QTc interval. He was transferred to the hospital ward where he continued to receive calcium (10 mmol/24 hours) intravenously and alphacalcidol (1 ug) orally. After 5 days, his plasma calcium normalised (2.15 mmol/L) together with normalisation of his creatine kinase level, and he was discharged.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old man presented with a 3-month progressive course of hoarseness, episodes of sudden speechlessness (8 times daily, 30-40 seconds duration), dyspnea, vomiting after swallowing cold water, and hand spasms/cramps during driving. Physical examination revealed positive Chvostek's and Trousseau's signs indicating neuromuscular irritability. Initial laboratory workup showed severe hypocalcemia (total calcium 1.03 mmol/L), hyperphosphatemia (2.21 mmol/L), hypomagnesemia (0.58 mmol/L), elevated CK (2962 IU/L), normal albumin, and normal renal/liver function. Subsequent testing confirmed low PTH (0.7 pmol/L) and low vitamin D3 (11 nmol/L), with ECG showing prolonged QTc interval (501 ms). Molecular investigations ruled out CaSR mutations and parathyroid antibodies, establishing idiopathic primary hypoparathyroidism. The patient was treated with intravenous calcium gluconate and magnesium sulphate in the emergency department with immediate improvement in voice. He was admitted and continued on intravenous calcium (total 20 mmol over 24 hours, then 10 mmol/24 hours) and alphacalcidol (1 μg orally) with cholecalciferol supplementation. After 24 hours, plasma calcium improved to 1.57 mmol/L with normalization of QTc interval. After 5 days of treatment, plasma calcium normalized to 2.15 mmol/L, CK normalized, and the patient was discharged.
